scenario.summary: Aeternum is a C++ botnet loader that utilizes the Polygon blockchain as a decentralized C2 infrastructure by querying smart contracts for encrypted instructions. The malware maintains persistence via Windows startup shortcuts and performs data exfiltration using the Telegram API, occasionally dropping additional threats like XWorm and XMRig miners.

meta.rationale: The hunt focuses on Windows endpoints. Scoping uses a broad check for Microsoft software to identify the estate.
meta.hypothesis: An adversary has established persistence via a startup shortcut pointing to a binary in a user-writable directory, which then executes multi-stage loaders and miners.

hunt.name: Aeternum Botnet: Persistence and Payload Deployment
hunt.description: This hunt targets the host-side lifecycle of the Aeternum botnet. It begins by scoping to Windows-based assets, then simultaneously searches for the creation of startup shortcuts and rare process executions in user-writable paths like AppData. Finally, it corroborates these behavioral signals against known loader and impact binary names (XWorm, XMRig) mentioned in research.

config.content: SELECT DISTINCT device_hostname FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE (LOWER(vendor_name) LIKE '%microsoft%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%windows%')
config.description: Aeternum is a Windows-centric botnet; this step narrows the estate to hosts running Microsoft software.
config.expected_signal: A list of hostnames belonging to the Windows estate. Silence here means no Windows assets were found, which would render the rest of the hunt irrelevant.

primitive_config.label: Identify Windows Assets
primitive_config.content: SELECT DISTINCT device_hostname FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE (LOWER(vendor_name) LIKE '%microsoft%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%windows%')
primitive_config.expected: A list of hostnames belonging to the Windows estate. Silence here means no Windows assets were found, which would render the rest of the hunt irrelevant.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, file_path, file_name, actor_user_name, time FROM hb_file_activity WHERE LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%\programs\startup\%' AND LOWER(file_name) LIKE '%.lnk' AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Find .lnk files created in the Startup directory, a common persistence technique for the Aeternum loader.
config.expected_signal: Shortcuts created in the startup folder. Most shortcuts here are benign; context provided by the other steps will isolate the threat.

primitive_config.label: New Startup Shortcuts
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, file_path, file_name, actor_user_name, time FROM hb_file_activity WHERE LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%\programs\startup\%' AND LOWER(file_name) LIKE '%.lnk' AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
primitive_config.expected: Shortcuts created in the startup folder. Most shortcuts here are benign; context provided by the other steps will isolate the threat.

config.content: SELECT LOWER(process_path) AS path, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS hosts, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_process_activity WHERE LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%\appdata\local\%' AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY 1 HAVING hosts < 3
config.description: Identify binaries running from user-writable AppData paths that are rare across the fleet.
config.expected_signal: Binaries running from local user profiles seen on very few hosts. Legitimate software (like Teams or Discord) will typically appear across many hosts.

primitive_config.label: Rare Processes in AppData

primitive_config.expected: Binaries running from local user profiles seen on very few hosts. Legitimate software (like Teams or Discord) will typically appear across many hosts.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_cmd_line, user_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (instr(',' || '{{known_binaries}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(process_name) || ',') > 0 OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%xmrig%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%xworm%') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
